about: The asset gate's rules (tools/asset_gate.py; docs/asset-rules.md is generated from this file). Kinds are derived from each model's facts, first match wins. Limits: a value above `warn` warns, above `fail` fails (`compare: min`: below). The Rust side embeds this file (src/asset_rules.rs).

kinds.name: Weapon (held)
kinds.why: Held weapons are seen in first person filling a third of the screen and in third person in a hand: they get hero triangle density on a small surface, a few more materials than a prop, and their pivot is the main-hand grip (the engine attaches it to a hand socket), so the bottom-centre origin, float and sink checks don't apply. Their moving parts are separate nodes driven by named glTF clips (fire, reload, draw...).

kinds.name: Landmark / superstructure
kinds.why: A city-scale hero structure (a kilometre-high tower): one per world, seen from everywhere. It gets its own budgets on purpose instead of breaking the building ones; it must ship a lean `collision` node so its walk-in collider stays small, and it relies on the engine's distance LODs (model_render::lod) far away. Its rooms are furnished with instanced copies of a few dozen pieces (each piece is also its own model): repeated mesh+material pairs draw as GPU instances, so its primitive and material budgets are sized for a furnished hotel rather than one building, while its unique triangles stay capped.

walker.source: src/motion/collide.rs Body::WALKER and movement.rs ground_move (floor disc = radius x 0.7)

walk.note: Floors are flat (within 41°) span tops more than 0.25 m up with room to stand. Regions smaller than min_floor_m2 are ignored, and so is furniture: a region less than furniture.below_m above the floor under it and smaller than furniture.max_m2 (beds, tables, counters). A floor neither walker reaches has no way up drawn (roofs, decorative decks) and is exempt.

rules.name: Triangles drawn
rules.why: Every triangle is drawn each frame the model is on screen, and again in each shadow cascade: budgets per kind keep a whole village at frame rate.

rules.name: Triangles in memory (scenes)
rules.why: A scene's pieces are instanced: what it keeps in memory and uploads is its unique triangles.

rules.name: Triangle density
rules.why: Detail the eye can't see at the distance the model is seen from: tiny triangles shade four times over; a 1.6 m bed at 5,600/m² is ten times denser than any hand-painted prop.

rules.name: Materials
rules.why: Each material is at least one more draw call and pipeline state per copy.

rules.name: Draw primitives
rules.why: Each primitive drawn (every instance of every mesh) is a draw call, before batching.

rules.name: Largest own texture
rules.why: Textures only this model (or its set) uses cost memory for it alone; shared library textures are free.

rules.name: Own texture memory
rules.why: Megapixels of textures nobody else shares: what loading this model adds to video memory.

rules.name: Own textures
rules.why: Many one-off textures usually mean a material set that should have come from the shared library.

rules.name: Missing textures
rules.why: A texture the model points at isn't there: it renders untextured (and other engines refuse it).

rules.name: Origin at the bottom centre
rules.why: Models are placed, turned and snapped by their origin: off-centre pivots swing wide when turned (wall and hanging pieces pivot on their fixing and are exempt).

rules.name: Bottom at the origin
rules.unit: m between the origin and the model's bottom, above it
rules.why: A model whose bottom is above its origin floats when placed on the ground (wall and hanging pieces pivot on their fixing and are exempt).

rules.name: Not mostly below the origin
rules.unit: share of the height below the origin
rules.why: Sinking a base into the ground is fine (a ship's hull below the waterline, a crypt stair, a rock's roots); most of a model below its origin means the pivot isn't at its bottom.

rules.name: Plausible size (metres)
rules.why: Larger than any building or ship: usually centimetres exported as metres.

rules.name: Plausible size (metres)
rules.why: Smaller than a coin: usually millimetres, or metres exported as centimetres the wrong way.

rules.name: Y-up, metres, as declared
rules.why: The glTF's real bounds must match the size its manifest or build stats declare: a Z-up export, a unit slip or a stray root transform shows up here.

rules.name: Welded vertices
rules.why: An unwelded mesh (a triangle soup) carries three vertices a triangle instead of about one: three times the memory and vertex work.

rules.name: Duplicate vertices
rules.why: Vertices identical in every attribute should be one vertex.

rules.name: Degenerate triangles
rules.why: Zero-area triangles cost a draw slot each and break normals, colliders and other engines' importers.

rules.name: One primitive per material
rules.why: A mesh with two primitives of the same material draws twice what could be drawn once.

rules.name: Repeated pieces instanced
rules.why: Identical meshes stored more than once: a scene must instance one mesh per piece.

rules.name: Unused materials
rules.why: Materials nothing draws still get loaded and exported.

rules.name: Unused images
rules.why: Images no used material samples still ship and may still load.

rules.name: Points and lines
rules.why: Point and line primitives aren't drawn as surfaces by the engine or most exporters.

rules.name: Collider size
rules.why: Walkable models collide with every triangle: the column grid near the player is rasterised from all of them.

rules.name: Floors with a way up are reachable
rules.why: A floor the drawn stairs, steps or ramps lead to that the walker (0.32 m radius, 1.8 m tall, 0.45 m steps) can't reach: too steep, too tight or too low on the way.

rules.name: Floors with a way up are reachable (open models)
rules.why: Like walk_floors, for walkable models that aren't walk-in (they collide as solid columns).

rules.name: Doors are passable
rules.why: A walk-size door the walker can't get through on both sides: the opening behind the leaf is too narrow or too low, or blocked.

lint.why: A set module may import only the library (hp_lib, hp_parts, hp_props, hp_buildings, hp_chest, hp_grave, hp_kit): importing another set's module ties two builds together, so one mid-edit breaks the other.
Adding to MATS at import time changes the shared material set for every build that happens to import the module: materials belong in hp_lib.MATS (or hp_kit).
mathutils noise.noise_vector is reseeded per Blender process, so builds stop being byte-identical: use three noise.noise lookups like Asset.wobble.
The random module's global functions and an unseeded random.Random() differ run to run: draw from the asset's seeded rng (Asset.rng; Asset.replay_rng restores a state).
A bmesh op fed from a set (a set comprehension, set(...), {…}) gets its elements in hash order, which changes run to run: keep order with dict.fromkeys(...).

mounted.about: Models whose pivot is deliberately not at their bottom centre, declared because the gate's shape guess (wall back face, hanging top) can't tell. wall / hanging: pivot on the fixing (no origin, float or sink checks); footed: pivot at the foot of a post, wall line or corner with the rest reaching out (no origin check); sunken: sits into the ground (no sink check). Moving these pivots would shift every placed copy in existing worlds.
